Sydney real estate spin frames a $1.8M inner-city auction as a 'buyers' market' while interest rate hikes lock out ordinary families.
Evidence: $1.8M clearance, agent spin, RBA rate hikes
#Sydney #RealEstate #Aletheia

Real estate agents and domain columns claim high interest rates have created a prime buyers' market where first home buyers can easily snap up inner-city properties.

Two bidders withdrew over loan affordability, yet the three-bedroom home cleared $1.803M above reserve. Calling seven-figure debt for the top 5% a 'buyers' market' is pure industry spin.

The Reserve Bank raised rates to 4.85%, causing two of four scheduled bidders to drop out over finance at an Alexandria auction. The property still beat its $1.75M reserve, selling for $1.803M.

Normalizing $1.8 million entry prices as accessible bargains forces desperate buyers into massive mortgage exposure while insulating developer and agent commissions from reality.
The audit exposes a fundamental plane error: confusing corporate marketing narrative (Q4 Lyrical) with physical economic affordability (Q3 Physical). Spin cannot lower repayments.

The real estate industry runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver. By declaring a 'buyers' market' amid rate hikes, agents manufacture artificial urgency to protect transaction momentum, leaving indebted buyers holding the long-term risk.
